mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen every week for four consecutive weeks (-20.6 to -11.7), indicating a steady return of office commuting. This recovering commuter base is expected to raise incidental weekday retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES increased monotonically from -20.6 to -11.7 across the four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than the prior 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stayed deeply suppressed and essentially flat around -1 to -3 for four weeks, well below pre-pandemic baseline. If TRANSIT fails to rise above -1.0 for the coming week, it signals commuting and errand-linked trips remain capped, limiting near-term retail visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -1.0 for the next observed week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT values ranged from -2.9 to -0.4 and ended at -1.3, showing no sustained breakout above -1.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week even though TRANSIT stays below -1.0, falsifying the capping mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES is rising (-20.6 to -11.7) while TRANSIT stays nearly flat near -1 to -3, implying commuters are returning to offices without a matching rise in public transit use, consistent with private vehicle or short-distance work-from-near-home patterns. This mismatch suggests discretionary retail trips tied to transit-based errands will not grow proportionally, suppressing RETAIL_REC gains.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 5 points while TRANSIT changes less than 2 points over the same period
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES gained ~8.9 points over four weeks while TRANSIT moved only within a 2.5-point band
regime_hint: partial reopening with weak transit recovery
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean rises over the next 28 days despite the WORKPLACES-TRANSIT divergence persisting, rejecting the decoupling mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has remained deeply negative (around -20) through four winter weeks in Delhi, consistent with cold-weather suppression of outdoor leisure. In this winter regime, reduced outdoor activity does not substitute into indoor retail and recreation visits, keeping RETAIL_REC subdued over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed between -19.9 and -21.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days rises above the prior 14-day mean while PARKS remains at or below -19, contradicting the seasonal suppression link.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed stable near +5 for four weeks with no upward spike, indicating no new stay-at-home policy tightening is underway. In this no-new-restriction regime, the absence of residential surges implies continued gradual normalization of retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed within a narrow 4.6 to 5.3 band across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days falls even though RESIDENTIAL remains flat near +5, rejecting the policy-stability-implies-retail-growth link.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has plateaued near +20 for four weeks, suggesting essential shopping demand is saturated. candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within a 2-point band for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM varied only between 19.9 and 21.0 over the four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean does not rise over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining plateaued within a narrow band.

evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -14.1 to -11.7 and TRANSIT rose from -1.1 to -1.3 range over the last two weeks

evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC stayed within a narrow -13.3 to -12.6 band across the four snapshot weeks
